messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>

Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>

Subject: Sprint Zero: App integration orchestration + SDK/endpoint migration plan

Hi Elliot —

Thanks again for the call this morning. As promised, here’s a concise "Sprint Zero" plan to get Apex Retail from POC to first-servered integration with Redwood:

1) Goals for Sprint Zero (1 week):
- SDK install and sample app running in your staging environment (Node + Go snippets)
- Endpoint migration rehearsal (old endpoint -> Redwood shim) with a canary route
- Retry/backoff and rate-limit policy validated against 10k synthetic requests
- Telemetry and tracing hooks confirmed (X-Request-ID propagation)

2) Key technical notes (what we recommend):
- SDK: use our 1.8.x client; default timeout 8s for generation calls, 2s for health probes.
- Retries: idempotent requests only (embeddings, non-stateful rerank) use exponential backoff with jitter: base=200ms, factor=2, max=5 attempts.
- Rate limits: client-side leaky-bucket at 300 qps for user-facing endpoints; token-level batching for high-throughput inference.
- Endpoint migration: implement a transparent shim that sends 10% traffic to Redwood (canary) for 24h, then 100% after validation.

3) Deliverables we’ll attach to this thread: sprint-zero MAP (mutual action plan), SDK snippet bundle, rate-limit cheatsheet.

Action items:
- Elliot: confirm sandbox cluster url + a service account for API key rotation by EOD Thu.
- Monica: we’ll ship the Go/Node snippets and the canary routing template by tomorrow.
- Vivek: I’ll prepare the commercial touchpoint for procurement (one-pager + expected usage).

If that aligns, we’ll spin up a dedicated Slack channel and a daily 15m stand for the week.

Cheers,

—Marissa

Elliot — thanks, quick answers inline below and a proposed implementation checklist.

Circuit breaker / health checks:
- Error threshold: 0.8% (5xx or malformed response) over a 1min sliding window triggers circuit-open for 30s.
- Latency threshold: 95th percentile > 2.5x baseline -> open for 60s and reduce canary to 0%.
- Probe: /v1/health -> 200 + latency under 200ms; we recommend the shim call this every 5s.

Timeout guidance (frontend 4s):
- For UI flows keep synchronous calls below 3.5s (allow 500ms buffer). We suggest offloading long generations to async jobs with polling/webhooks.

Implementation checklist (Sprint Zero) — target owners:
- [Elliot] Create sandbox service account + share key.
- [Elliot/Impl] Stand up shim proxy (we can provide a NGINX-config + sample) to switch traffic percentages.
- [Monica] Provide SDK snippets (Node: fetch-based; Go: context-aware client) and sample test harness for 10k synthetic QPS.
- [Marissa] Create Slack channel and schedule daily 15m sync (09:00 PDT).

I’ve uploaded the NGINX canary template and a small test harness to the Drive link in this thread.

—Monica
Monica Patel | Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Elliot — quick commercial / procurement note to keep things moving.

1) Usage estimate: based on your POC we’ll model ~6M tokens/mo to start. I’ll share a straightforward committed tier that reduces per-token price and includes a Dedicated burst window for Black Friday prep.
2) Procurement checklist:

Operational note for the engineers: when you flip from canary -> 100% traffic, please perform a KV-cache warmup (run the common 50k prefixes warmup job; script included in sdk_samples). That reduces latency spikes on first cold requests.

If the team signs off on the Sprint Zero MAP I’ll coordinate a signed SOW and get the procurement one-pager over.

Thanks — Vivek
